name: aaaflow studio
summary: a local-first video studio connecting scripts, voices, generated visuals, and final video assembly on a consumer gpu. a voice-first pipeline with channel personas shaped by prompts; two resulting videos are published on youtube.
problem: Bring the steps of making a narrated video into one workspace: script, voice, visuals, editing, preview, and export. The timeline follows the actual narration so scenes stay aligned with what is being said.
highlights: Voice-led timing: Generate narration per scene and use the resulting audio duration to drive the timeline, instead of forcing speech into a fixed scene length.
Connected creative tools: Combine local speech and image generation, ComfyUI workflows, animation, and final video assembly in a browser-based studio.
Channel identity: Channel personas, visual prompts, and editing presets help keep a project's outputs consistent. Voice Lab and per-scene editing provide room to refine the result.

sections.heading: The workflow
sections.body:
- Start with a storyboard and channel direction.
- Generate narration and build the audio-led timeline.
- Generate or refine visuals and edit the scene sequence.
- Preview the assembled video and prepare the final export.

sections.heading: Under the hood
sections.body: A JavaScript interface talks to Python/FastAPI services that coordinate model inference, background jobs, project storage, and media processing. The larger workflow integrates ComfyUI, local models, Remotion, and FFmpeg.

sections.heading: Scope & current state
sections.body: A local-first personal production tool with two published videos. Model setup, GPU memory, and generation time affect the experience; online publishing and external services are separate from local inference.
